definition.value: heroin-related vs. rest during the early scan period

value: For the early scan, there was significant brain activation to heroin-related cues in left VTA, thalamus, hippocampus, OFC, ventral caudate/NAc, superior occipital gyrus and precentral gyrus, right postcentral gyrus, inferior temporal gyrus and lingual gyrus, bilateral amygdala, superior parietal lobule and inferior frontal gyrus.
These regions are known to play critical roles in reward, reinforcement, control, motivation, drive, learning, and memory.

definition.value: heroin-related vs. rest during the late scan period

value: For the late scan, there was significant brain activation to heroin-related cues in left postcentral gyrus, supramarginal gyrus, superior parietal lobule and middle occipital gyrus, right OFC, inferior temporal gyrus and inferior parietal lobule, and bilateral inferior frontal gyrus.
Unlike in the early scan, there was no activation in VTA, thalamus, amygdala, hippocampus and ventral caudate/NAc in the late scan.

definition.value: brain activation to heroin-related cues was significantly greater for the early scan compared to the late scan

spans.text: The time of study was held constant for all participants at 13:00 to 15:00 pm .

value: Direct comparison between the two scans showed that brain activation to heroin-related cues was significantly greater for the early scan in left VTA, thalamus, paracentral lobule, middle temporal gyrus and calcarine sulcus, right amygdala, hippocampus, precentral gyrus and postcentral gyrus, compared to the late scan.

Brain regions showing reduced fMRI response to heroin-related cues from early to late periods include VTA, thalamus, amygdala, hippocampus, paracentral lobule, precentral gyrus, postcentral gyrus, middle temporal gyrus and calcarine sulcus. These brain regions may be related to the desire for heroin due to negative reinforcement and can be modulated by buprenorphine as therapeutic targets.
